headline: Tabled a veterans' housing concept plan for 200 Trapelo Road and an artificial intelligence resolution; asked IT Director for report on city AI use.
summary: A concept plan for veterans' housing and services at 200 Trapelo Road was presented and tabled. A resolution on artificial intelligence was discussed, and the IT Director was asked for a report on current AI use and policies. The AI resolution was then tabled.
decisions: Tabled the concept plan for veterans' housing and services at 200 Trapelo Road, by voice vote.
Approved a request for the IT Director to provide the Council with current AI usage and any practices or policies in place, by voice vote.
Tabled the resolution concerning artificial intelligence (AI), by voice vote.

transcript:
# Committee of the Whole

Minutes of the Meeting

Monday - September 21, 2026

1. VP LeBlanc called the meeting to Order at 8:00pm in the City Council Chamber.

2. VP LeBlanc requested that a roll call be taken to record the attendance for the meeting. The COW Clerk called the roll - Councillors Bradley-MacArthur, Dunn, Durkee, Hanley, Harris, King, LaCava, LaFauci, President Logan, McLaughlin, Tzioumis, Vidal and VP LeBlanc were all present in-person. Councillors Brasco and Katz were absent.

3. President Logan moved to approve the minutes of the COW meeting held on August 3, 2026. The motion was adopted on a voice vote and the minutes of the COW meeting on August 3, 2026 were approved.

4. A request was received from the Mayor to present a concept plan for veterans' housing and services at the 200 Trapelo Road property. A motion to hear from the following individuals was adopted on a voice vote - Mayor McCarthy, Purchasing Agent Crystal Philpott, Caritas Executive Director Frank Connell, Veterans Pathways CEO Jason Gilbert, BWA Architecture Principal David Tanner and Commodore Builders Commercial Group Leader Dan Hudd. Ms. Philpott gave an introductory statement stating the veterans housing would be utilizing the Dolan and McDougall Buildings. Mr. Connell gave an overview of the project and Mr. Gilbert explained the benefits that would be provided to veterans. Mr. Tanner distributed a handout and gave a PowerPoint presentation explaining the goal of the project, the status of the buildings to be utilized and the layout of the floor space. The Mayor stated there would be a lease with Caritas for the property management. Councillor McLaughlin stated his support for the project and emphasized the need for Waltham veterans to be given priority. Councillor McLaughlin asked about the timeline for the project. Mr. Connell explained the need for state approval of the funding would be determining factor - likely 2027 or 2028. Councillor McLaughlin asked about the condition of the two buildings, to which Mr. Tanner stated it needed further investigation. Councillor Hanley stated his support for the project and asked questions about eligibility criteria for tenants, transportation needs and anyway to speed up the process. Councillor Bradley MacArthur asked several follow up questions about eligibility and turnover. The Mayor stated access to the property would be from Waverly Oaks Road. President Logan asked questions about the duration of the lease and he supported the project. Councillor LaFauci asked questions about security for the property and the length of stay for a tenant. Councillor Harris stated the need to prioritize Waltham veterans, the experience with this type of property and the sources of income for the tenant's rent obligation. Councillor Durkee asked several questions about the funding sources to rehab the property and if there would be a cost to the City. Councillor Durkee also questioned the size of the unit at about 300 square feet, stating it was small and not adequate. Councillor Tzioumis asked if the property would be for families and its energy efficiency. Mr. Connell stated the tenancy would be for individuals only. Councillor King stated his support for the project an also emphasized the need to give priority to Waltham veterans. Councillor Dunn asked about on-site supervision and the hours it would be in effect. The presenters were thanked for their explanation of the project and Councillor McLaughlin moved to table the matter. The motion was adopted on a voice vote.

5. A resolution concerning Artificial Intelligence (AI) was submitted by Councillor Vidal. Councillor Vidal move to hear from the IT Director, Donnie Aucoin. The motion was adopted on a voice vote. Councillor Vidal opened the discussion asking if the City was suing AI. Mr. Aucoin stated yes, but it was in the infancy stage, using it primarily for e-mail and other correspondence. Councillor Vidal asked several follow up questions concerning the impact or concerns with cyber security, any areas to look at, and if AI is being used by our software vendors. Mr. Aucoin suggested forming a steering committee for AI. Councillor Bradley-MacArthur asked several follow up questions and moved to request the IT Director provide the Council with the current usage of AI and any practices/policies in place. The motion was adopted on a voice vote. Councillor King asked several questions about restrictions with AI and if we are putting our information into cyberspace. Councillor Dunn asked if the City should hire an AI consultant. Councillor McLaughlin asked if there are any resources available, either from the State and/or other communities. Mr. Aucoin stated that AI was not an IT Department issue but a community issue and needed involvement from local leaders. Councillor Vidal moved to place the matter on the table. The motion was adopted on a voice vote.

6. A motion by Councillor McLaughlin to adjourn was adopted on a voice vote and VP LeBlanc declared the meeting adjourned at 10:07pm.

Paul G. Centofanti – Clerk to the Committee of the Whole
